name: SJAVS
description: Sjavs (pronounced 'Shows' or 'Shavs') is a popular card game in the Faroe Islands and parts of Denmark. It is a derivative of the German game Schafkopf, played with a stripped deck of 32 cards (standard Skat/Piquet deck). The game involves bidding, trump calling, and trick-taking, with a unique scoring system based on 'Rubbers' (first to reach 0 points from 24). It is highly strategic and social.

content.text: Sjavs (pronounced 'Shows' or 'Shavs') is a popular card game in the Faroe Islands and parts of Denmark. It is a derivative of the German game Schafkopf, played with a stripped deck of 32 cards (standard Skat/Piquet deck). The game involves bidding, trump calling, and trick-taking, with a unique scoring system based on 'Rubbers' (first to reach 0 points from 24). It is highly strategic and social.
Introduced to the Faroe Islands by Danish merchants or sailors familiar with German Schafkopf. The name 'Sjavs' likely comes from *Schafkopf*.

32 cards: the 2s through 6s are removed from a standard 52-card pack. Six cards are permanent highest trumps (Club Q, Spade Q, Club J, Spade J, Heart J, Diamond J); remaining cards rank A, K, Q, 10, 9, 8, 7. Point values: A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2; 120 points in the pack.

32 cards: the 2s through 6s are removed from a standard 52-card pack. Six cards are permanent highest trumps (Club Q, Spade Q, Club J, Spade J, Heart J, Diamond J); remaining cards rank A, K, Q, 10, 9, 8, 7. Point values: A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2; 120 points in the pack.

items.text: Suðuroy (Southern island): If pack is cut, deal 3-2-3 instead of 4-4. If 60-60, next game value increases by 2 or 4 depending on winner. Many do not award double victory if losers still on 24, or extra points for single player winning all tricks.

Three-player Sjavs: 10 cards each, 2 to table face down. Bidding same; one player makes trumps and plays alone vs the other two. Trump maker may discard one or two cards and pick up from table. Three columns on score sheet; soloist subtracts on win, opponents each subtract on loss.

Two-player Sjavs: Four face-down and four face-up cards per player in rows, plus 8 cards in hand. Face-up count as hand; when a table card is played the one under it is turned up. Bidding up to 12 possible.
